title: Middleware and Request Context knowledge check

questions.prompt: What belongs in a production backend type boundary?
options: Validate requests, authorize the action on the server, handle failures and preserve data-integrity invariants.
Trust a client TypeScript interface as an access-control mechanism.
Log credentials so failed requests can be reproduced.
questions.answer_key: Validate requests, authorize the action on the server, handle failures and preserve data-integrity invariants.
questions.explanation: Backend runtime behavior and authorization must be enforced on the server, independent of client types.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Middleware and Request Context”?
options: The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with middleware contracts and checked against its intended contract.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with middleware contracts and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Middleware contracts”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Middleware and Request Context”?
options: Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check request-specific state, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume authentication context and request validation is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
questions.answer_key: Check request-specific state, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Request-specific state”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
